title: TypeScript SDK: refactor retry + timeout plumbing to match SDK standard (incl. AbortController + streaming)
creator: Ibrahim Khan
content:
## Context
We need to eliminate TS-specific retry/timeout behavior drift that’s causing “works in TS but not Python/Go” incidents. This ticket is the TypeScript refactor work to:
- centralize retry + timeout logic in a single request pipeline
- align with the company SDK retry/timeout standards + ADRs
- ensure streaming semantics are safe (no surprise replays) and cancellation is reliable
- preserve backwards compatibility where feasible (or provide deprecation path)

Primary drivers:
- Support escalations around TS retrying non-retryable errors (e.g., 400) and inconsistent Retry-After handling
- Confusion about what “timeout” means (overall vs connect/read) and how it interacts with streaming
- Inconsistent request_id propagation into errors, making oncall/support triage slow

## Goals
1) One unified place that decides:
   - is an error retryable?
   - how long to wait (exp backoff + jitter / Retry-After)
   - when to abort (timeouts/cancellation)
2) Consistent config surface across SDKs (names + defaults) and consistent error fields.
3) Streaming handling:
   - AbortController cancellation should reliably stop fetch + reader
   - no automatic retry after we have received any response bytes/events
   - if a failure happens before first byte, retry can occur if policy allows

## Non-goals
- Redesigning public API methods or streaming event shapes (handled in separate streaming parity tickets)
- Adding new auth mechanisms

## Proposed/Implemented design
### Retry
- Implement `RetryPolicy` + `RetryMiddleware` as the single authority for retry classification and scheduling.
- Retryable categories (per standard):
  - HTTP 429 (respect `Retry-After`)
  - HTTP 5xx (except where explicitly terminal)
  - network/connection failures (DNS, ECONNRESET, socket hang up, fetch `TypeError` where applicable)
- Non-retryable:
  - 4xx (except 429); especially ensure we do NOT retry 400/401/403/404/409/422
- Max attempts:
  - default attempts aligned to standard (1 initial + N retries). We kept naming in code as `maxAttempts` to be unambiguous.
- Backoff:
  - exponential backoff with jitter; cap to avoid retry storms
  - always honor `Retry-After` when present (both delta-seconds and HTTP-date formats)

### Timeouts
- Standardize on an explicit timeout model that maps cleanly to fetch:
  - `timeout`: overall request timeout (ms)
  - optional `connectTimeout` / `readTimeout` are *not* truly representable in fetch; we emulate read/idle timeout for streaming by tracking time since last byte.
- Default timeouts (as shipped for parity):
  - Non-streaming overall timeout: 60,000ms
  - Streaming overall timeout: 900,000ms
  - Streaming idle/read timeout (time since last chunk): 60,000ms
- Implementation detail:
  - merge user-provided `AbortSignal` with an internal `AbortController` used for timeouts
  - ensure abort reasons are preserved where possible and surfaced in typed errors (without leaking secrets)

### Streaming interaction
- Before first byte:
  - retry allowed if policy says retryable (e.g., 429/5xx, network failure).
- After first byte/event:
  - no automatic retry; surface a `StreamingDisconnectError` (typed) with `request_id` if available.
  - docs/migration notes recommend idempotency keys for safe retries at the application level.

## Backwards compatibility plan
We preserved old option names where possible and added warnings:
- Support legacy option aliases (e.g., `timeoutMs`, `maxRetries`) mapped to new config.
- If both legacy + new are provided, precedence is explicit new option > legacy alias.
- Deprecated option usage prints one warning per process (guarded) with a link to migration notes.

Behavior changes called out in migration notes:
- TS no longer retries 400-series responses (except 429)
- Retry-After is respected (reduces immediate rapid retries)
- Streaming abort/cancellation is more aggressive and consistent (previously could hang on some runtimes)

## Acceptance criteria
- [x] All request paths (non-streaming + streaming) share the same retry + timeout code.
- [x] 429 handling:
  - respects `Retry-After` for both seconds and HTTP-date
  - surfaces `retryable=true` on errors
- [x] Does not retry on 400/401/403/404/409/422.
- [x] Error objects include `request_id` when present (response header or body field), plus `status_code` where applicable.
- [x] Streaming cancellation:
  - `abort()` stops iteration promptly and closes reader
  - partial output is preserved up to the last received chunk
- [x] Unit/integration tests cover:
  - retry classification table
  - backoff scheduling and caps
  - timeout abort path
  - streaming disconnect path and “no retry after first byte” guard

## Implementation checklist (review)
- [x] Centralize retry logic (no per-endpoint retry decisions).
- [x] Ensure retry waits are cancellable (abort while sleeping).
- [x] Ensure `Retry-After` parsing is RFC-compliant and handles invalid values safely.
- [x] Ensure retry attempts do not double-consume streams.
- [x] Ensure request bodies are replayable only when safe (JSON payloads OK; arbitrary streams not retried).
- [x] Ensure logging does not include API key or Authorization headers.
- [x] Ensure browser + Node runtimes behave similarly (fetch implementations differ; tests include both where possible).

## Links
- TS PR (retry middleware + error shapes): sources/github/redwood-sdk-typescript/pr-1298-unify-retry-middleware-and-error-shapes.json
- TS PR (timeouts + AbortController plumbing): sources/github/redwood-sdk-typescript/pr-1302-timeouts-defaults-and-abortcontroller-plumbing.json
- TS PR (Retry-After parsing + jitter): sources/github/redwood-sdk-typescript/pr-1307-retry-after-parsing-and-backoff-jitter.json
- Standard/ADR references:
  - sources/confluence/architecture-and-standards/api-standards/sdk-retry-timeout-standard.json
  - sources/confluence/architecture-and-standards/decision-records/adr-sdk-retry-policy-v1.json
  - sources/confluence/architecture-and-standards/decision-records/adr-sdk-timeout-model.json

## Notes / follow-ups
- Conformance suite will be the gate for ongoing parity (ENG-5127). This ticket added targeted unit tests but the shared fixtures are tracked separately.
- Platform dependency: consistent `Retry-After` on 429 and consistent `request_id` (ENG-5130 / gateway PRs) — we still handle missing headers gracefully.
comments: 2026-01-17 (Dana Lo): Did a pass through current middleware stack. Retry logic is duplicated: one in core client wrapper and one in chat/streaming helper. Plan is to build a single `requestWithPolicy()` used everywhere. Will keep legacy option names as aliases and add a migration warning (once per process).

2026-01-22 (Allison Grant): Please ensure Retry-After parsing supports both delta-seconds and HTTP-date; cap max delay to avoid clients waiting for hours on malformed values. Also make sure retry sleeps are abortable so user cancellation is responsive.

2026-01-28 (Henry Cho): PM request: keep defaults conservative to avoid retry storms; messaging should emphasize that 429 will now back off more correctly and that 4xx non-429 won’t retry. Also add request_id to error surfaces for support macros.

2026-02-03 (Dana Lo): Implemented unified retry middleware + error shape propagation. Verified we no longer retry 400 (regression test added). Next: timeouts + AbortController wiring for streaming; we’ve seen hangs in Node when consumer stops reading early.

2026-02-07 (Marcus Lin): Security note: ensure debug logging does not print Authorization. Also ensure thrown errors don’t echo token values (some fetch errors can include request headers in certain wrappers). Please scrub/avoid dumping request objects in errors.

2026-02-11 (Dana Lo): Timeouts refactor complete. We now merge user AbortSignal with internal timeout controller. Added streaming idle timeout watchdog (time since last chunk). Confirmed cancellation exits iterator within one tick in Node 18 + undici fetch.

2026-02-14 (Ibrahim Khan): Review checklist: verify no streaming auto-retry after first byte; ensure Retry-After honored; confirm legacy options still work but warn. Please double-check attempt counting semantics match other SDKs (attempt=1 includes initial request).

2026-02-18 (Dana Lo): Final changes landed. Added Retry-After tests (seconds + date) and cap. Updated docsstrings in client options. Ready to mark done; conformance harness will validate cross-language alignment next.

2026-02-20 (Connor O'Brien): Coordinated release window with Python/Go. TS tagged for redwood-sdk-typescript@1.14.0 in the parity rollout batch; release notes will point to migration guide and emphasize changed retry behavior for 4xx.
